insurer: Aditya Birla Health Insurance Co. Limited
sumInsured: Base Sum Insured options: 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 7L, 10L, 15L, 20L, 25L, 50L, 75L, 1Cr, 2Cr, 3Cr, 4Cr, 5Cr, 6Cr (plus Super Reload, Super Credit, optional Cancer Booster etc. as applicable)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: Room Rent: Actuals up to Sum Insured
great.explanation: Room rent is payable at actuals up to the Sum Insured, with no daily cap or room-category restriction mentioned. This reduces the risk of out-of-pocket costs and avoids room-rent linked deductions.

great.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
great.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred... for up to 90 days immediately prior to the date of such Hospitalization.
great.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 90 days before admission for the same condition. This is better than the common 60-day window and helps cover diagnostics and consultations leading to hospitalization.

great.name: Consumables
great.quote: Non-payable items will be covered (all 4 lists of Annexure I)
great.reference: Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (SAVR) / Section C.4 Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver)
great.explanation: Non-payable consumables are covered as per all 4 lists in Annexure I under the Claim Protect benefit. This can significantly reduce out-of-pocket spend on items like gloves, masks, and procedure kits during hospitalization.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: We shall provide for a reload amounting to the Base Sum Insured (“Super Reload”), unlimited times during the Policy Year
great.explanation: A reload equal to the Base Sum Insured is available unlimited times in the same policy year once the cover is used. This is strong protection for multiple hospitalizations in a year.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: Super Credit (Increases Irrespective of Claim) ... An additional limit under the current Policy Year (“Super Credit”) will be applied / increased by a fixed percentage of the Base Sum Insured of immediately preceding Policy Year irrespective of any claims in previous Policy Year
great.reference: Section C.11 Super Credit / Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (SAVR)
great.explanation: An additional limit (“Super Credit”) increases by a fixed percentage of the prior year’s Base Sum Insured irrespective of claims. This helps your available cover grow even in years when you make claims.

great.name: Modern Treatments
great.quote: Expenses incurred... arising out of any of the below mentioned Indicative list of Modern Procedures / Treatments... Robotic Surgeries... Stereotactic Radio Surgeries... Stem Cell Therapy: Hematopoietic Stem Cells for Bone Marrow Transplant...
great.explanation: Modern procedures/treatments listed (including robotic surgeries and stereotactic radio surgeries) are covered as hospitalization expenses. This improves access to advanced care without needing a separate add-on.

great.name: Bariatric Surgery
great.quote: Obesity Treatment: Medical Expenses... arising out of Hospitalization for a Bariatric Surgery during the Policy Period subject to the conditions... Section D.1.6
great.explanation: Bariatric surgery is covered subject to the conditions mentioned in Section D.1.6. This can be valuable because many retail policies exclude weight-loss surgery unless explicitly covered.

great.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
great.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Medical Expenses incurred during the Policy Period on Domiciliary Hospitalization...
great.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization expenses are covered when treatment is taken at home as per the policy conditions. This helps when hospital admission is not possible or medically advised against.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Pre Existing Disease (PED) Waiting Period: 3 years
good.reference: Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (SAVR) - Waiting Period (Inbuilt Cover)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after a waiting period of 3 years (36 months). This is within the normal 2–4 year range seen in the market.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries / treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...
good.reference: Section D.1.2 Specified disease / procedure Waiting Period (Code-Excl02)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered until 24 months of continuous coverage are completed. This is a standard waiting period for such conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 30-day Waiting Period (Code-Excl03)... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness claims are not covered in the first 30 days from the first policy start date, while accidents are covered immediately. This is the usual initial waiting period structure.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred... for up to 180 days from the date of discharge from the Hospital.
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days after discharge for the same condition. This is at the upper end of standard post-hospitalization coverage.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Preferred Provider Network (PPN) Discount... If the Insured Person takes treatment... other than those listed as “Preferred Provider Network”, then... shall bear a Co-Payment of 10% on each and every claim
bad.reference: Section C.15.5 Preferred Provider Network (PPN) Discount
bad.explanation: A 10% co-payment applies on each and every claim if treatment is taken outside the Preferred Provider Network under the PPN Discount feature. This can materially increase your out-of-pocket costs whenever you use a non-PPN hospital.

unclear.name: No-claim Bonus
unclear.quote: If the feature from the table above is not found in the document, assume it is NOT covered and flag as BAD.
unclear.reference: NCB not expressly defined as NCB/Cumulative Bonus in the provided policy wording excerpts; Super Credit is a separate mechanism

unclear.name: Home Health Care
unclear.quote: This Benefit requires pre-authorisation and is not available on reimbursement basis.
unclear.explanation: Home Health Care is available only with pre-authorisation and is not payable on a reimbursement basis. This may limit usage if cashless/pre-authorisation is not feasible in your situation.
